scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

Relying on a tight-knit group for decision-making can offer significant support and a sense of community, particularly within a shared value system like a religious community. However, this reliance can impact self-trust when the group is not present. This balance can enhance confidence and capability in making decisions independently.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?

From what I understand, the family was hosting a Christmas party with around 20 people. The sister-in-law came to the party while she was having contractions and was clearly in labor. At first, it wasn't too bad, but as time went on, her contractions became more frequent and disruptive. She even screamed during one of the kids' present openings. The person who asked her to leave did so politely, suggesting it was time to go because they didn't want her to give birth in their kitchen. Her husband got angry, she called the person a bitch, and some of her family members left afterward. So, is it right or wrong to ask someone in labor to leave a family gathering? On one hand, the person wanted everyone to have a good day and didn't want the situation to become too distracting or uncomfortable. On the other hand, the sister-in-law was in a vulnerable state, and asking her to leave might have been insensitive or even cruel. I think it's important to consider the feelings of both parties. The person hosting the party had a responsibility to ensure that the gathering was enjoyable for everyone. If the sister-in-law's situation was making the event uncomfortable or stressful for others, it might have been reasonable to suggest she leave. However, the way it was handled could have been more compassionate. Maybe offering support or helping her get to the hospital instead of asking her to leave abruptly would have been better. Also, cultural and personal expectations play a role here. In some cultures, family gatherings are very important, and asking someone to leave could be seen as a significant breach of trust or respect. In other cultures, practicality might take precedence, and ensuring the well-being of the person in labor would be the priority. Another aspect to consider is the potential legal or medical implications. If someone is in labor, they should be under medical supervision. Encouraging or assisting her to go to the hospital might have been a better approach than asking her to leave the gathering without providing support. In conclusion, while the intention to maintain a pleasant family gathering is understandable, the method of asking her to leave might have been insensitive. A more compassionate and supportive approach, such as offering assistance to get her to the hospital, could have been a better way to handle the situation.
